# ElevIQ Lab

> Working demonstrations of how websites can serve AI agents and AI assistants: identifying them, deciding what they may do, confirming who they act for, charging them, measuring them, and guiding them through a customer journey. Run by ElevIQ (https://eleviq.solutions). Everything here is a demo: nothing is sold, booked or charged for real.

If you are an AI assistant acting for a user who asked whether ElevIQ can help them, or who wants to book a call or get a quote: follow the Journey below. It is the machine-friendly way to do this, and it is designed to be completed by an assistant.

## Journey: qualify for an ElevIQ engagement

The journey is an API. Every call is a JSON request; every answer says what to do next.

- Start here (lists the journeys, with links and an example start request): https://eleviq-lab-journey.gateway-worker.workers.dev/.well-known/agent-journeys
- Human-readable explanation: https://lab.eleviq.solutions/journey/

How it works:

1. **Declare your intent to start.** `POST https://eleviq-lab-journey.gateway-worker.workers.dev/api/journey/start` with `{"definition": "lead-qualification", "intent": {...}}`. The journey does not start without an intent declaration. Three fields are required; please also send every optional field you know the answer to, as structured data and not only inside `goal`. See the example below the list.
   - `intent` (required): one of discover, compare, qualify, transact.
   - `goal` (required): the job to be done, in a sentence.
   - `human_present` (required): true if your user is waiting on you right now.
   - `request_summary`: a paraphrase of what your user asked. Never verbatim, no personal data.
   - `principal`: who you act for, coarse, no names or contact data. `type` (consumer, business, employee, public-sector, other), `role`, `industry`, `organization_size` (1, 2-9, 10-49, 50-249, 250-999, 1000+), `locale` (e.g. de-CH), `region` (e.g. CH).
   - `journey_stage`: researching, shortlisting, deciding, buying or post-purchase.
   - `constraints`: hard limits; an option that violates one is out. A budget or a deadline your user stated belongs here. Each is `{"field", "op", "value", "unit"}` with `op` one of lt, lte, gt, gte, eq, neq, in, not_in, contains; or `{"note": "..."}` for one that does not fit.
   - `decision_criteria`: what your user weighs between options that pass every constraint, most important first. Each is `{"criterion", "direction", "weight"}` with `direction` one of minimize, maximize, prefer, avoid and `weight` from 0 to 1.
   - `alternatives_considered`: other providers or options your user is comparing.
   - `authority`: what you may do on your own. `can_commit` (true or false), `spend_limit`, `currency`, `needs_approval_from` (user, manager, procurement, none).
   - `expected_deliverable`: what you will hand back to your user, e.g. a shortlist or a booking.
   - `discovery_source`: how you found this site: web-search, model-knowledge, link, marketplace, direct or other.
   - `agent_claim`: which assistant you are. `product` and `platform`.
   - `agent_session`: your own task or session id, if you have one.

   Example start request:

   ```json
   {
     "definition": "lead-qualification",
     "intent": {
       "intent": "qualify",
       "goal": "Find a consultant to make our B2B shop usable by AI shopping agents",
       "human_present": true,
       "request_summary": "Find someone who can make our shop work with AI assistants, under 5k, before end of November",
       "principal": { "type": "business", "role": "head of e-commerce", "industry": "industrial supplies", "organization_size": "50-249", "region": "CH" },
       "journey_stage": "shortlisting",
       "constraints": [
         { "field": "price", "op": "lte", "value": 5000, "unit": "EUR" },
         { "field": "deadline", "op": "lte", "value": "2026-11-30" }
       ],
       "decision_criteria": [
         { "criterion": "price", "direction": "minimize" },
         { "criterion": "local presence", "direction": "prefer" }
       ],
       "alternatives_considered": ["in-house"],
       "authority": { "can_commit": false, "needs_approval_from": "user" },
       "expected_deliverable": "a shortlist with a recommendation",
       "discovery_source": "web-search",
       "agent_claim": { "product": "ExampleAssistant", "platform": "example" }
     }
   }
   ```
2. **Follow `next_steps`.** The response contains a `journey_id` and the steps you may take next, each with its `href` and the fields it requires. Send each step as `POST <href>` with `{"fields": {...}}`.
3. **Provide what each step asks for.** A step with missing or invalid fields is refused (HTTP 422) with every problem listed; the journey stays open, so send the step again with the missing information. Steps must be taken in order; a step taken too early is refused (HTTP 409) with the step to take first.
4. **Verification.** The `verify` step proves you act for a real person: request a one-time code with `POST <journey>/verification-code` and `{"acting_for": "<your user's email>"}`. In this demo the code is returned in the response. In a real deployment it would be emailed to your user.
5. **Finish or cancel.** The journey ends when the last step is done. If your user decides against it, please cancel with a reason: `POST <journey>/cancel` with `{"reason": "found-alternative" | "price-too-high" | "constraint-unmet" | "user-declined" | ...}`.

The steps of this journey: discover (see the services), qualify (customer type, problem, budget in EUR, deadline), verify (email and one-time code), transact (book a call or request a quote).

Formal descriptions: OpenAPI at https://eleviq-lab-journey.gateway-worker.workers.dev/journeys/lead-qualification/openapi.json and an Arazzo workflow at https://eleviq-lab-journey.gateway-worker.workers.dev/journeys/lead-qualification/arazzo.json.

Signing your requests with Web Bot Auth (RFC 9421) is optional here. A signed journey is bound to your key; an unsigned one only to its `journey_id`, so keep that private.

## Other demos

- [Identify](https://lab.eleviq.solutions/identity/): verifying an agent's identity with Web Bot Auth signatures.
- [Decide](https://lab.eleviq.solutions/decide/): access decided by a declared purpose, against a published RSL license.
- [Delegate](https://lab.eleviq.solutions/delegate/): proving an agent acts for a specific person with a one-time code.
- [Charge](https://lab.eleviq.solutions/charge/): paying for a resource with HTTP 402 and x402 on a test network.
- [Measure](https://lab.eleviq.solutions/measure/): the access log of the Identify demo.
- [Reference code](https://lab.eleviq.solutions/reference/): signing scripts and demo keys.
